data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts will produce more reliable judgments if the task's complexity is 'shallow' (decomposable into binary checks), but this is distinguishable from genuine reliability through the use of 'decoy' checklist items that track whether the panel is thinking or merely ticking.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task requires holistic synthesis that cannot be decomposed without losing critical information.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert's intuition is fundamentally a compressed version of the checklist's logic.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The checklist transforms a complex judgment task into a series of low-variance binary decisions, effectively filtering out the 'noise' of individual non-expert incompetence while simultaneously capping the 'ceiling' of possible insight.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
